data.description:
## Symptom

No workflow step runs `npx playwright install chromium`, so the `browser_runner` fixture self-skips on
"Chromium unavailable" in CI. **The browser test tier never actually runs there.**

Surfaced while implementing bug `9a17-e0b3-7aa6-4091`; pre-existing and untouched by that change.

## Why this matters more than a normal skip

A skipped tier is indistinguishable from a passing one in the summary line. CI reports green, and the
green is partly vacuous — nobody is told that a whole class of assertions never executed. That is the
same failure shape as two other defects found on 2026-09-04:

- `9a17`: provisioning cost was charged to a test budget, and the resulting worker kill reported as a
  crash rather than a timeout — the true cause was invisible in the summary.
- `90c7`: the `scanner-integration` job was added and **never ran** on the change that introduced it,
  yet that change still received `Verified +1`. A vote was cast on a job that did not execute.

In all three the gate said "fine" while not actually checking. This ticket is the mildest of the
three, but it is the same class: **absence of execution reported as success.**

Note also that change 2600 moved `playwright` to `optionalDependencies` and provisions with
`--omit=optional` for selections containing no browser test. That is correct and deliberate — it cut
the cold install from 15 packages / 30M to 11 / 12M. It does mean the browser path now needs
provisioning *explicitly* when it is wanted, rather than arriving incidentally.

## What needs deciding, and it is a real fork

Either:
- **(a) Run the tier in CI** — add a browser-provisioning step (`npx playwright install chromium`,
  plus its OS dependencies) so `browser_runner` actually executes. Costs CI minutes and adds a
  download to the critical path; the browser binary is large and would want caching.
- **(b) Keep it skipped, but make the skip LOUD and INTENTIONAL** — assert somewhere that the tier is
  deliberately not run in CI, so the skip is a recorded decision rather than an accident, and a
  future reader is not misled into thinking browser behaviour is covered.

**(b) is not a lesser option** and may well be right: the tier may be genuinely local-only by design.
What is not acceptable is the current state, where the skip is silent and looks like coverage.

Whichever is chosen must respect `project.portability` (a blocking plan-review criterion): the
behaviour cannot depend on a specific CI provider. A developer with no CI must get the same,
comprehensible result.

## Acceptance criteria

Deterministic, verifiable in one run.

1. The disposition is explicit and recorded in the tree: either the tier runs in CI, or a test/assert
   states that it is deliberately skipped there and why.
2. If (a): `browser_runner` tests actually execute in CI — demonstrated by a run where they report as
   passed rather than skipped, and the browser download is cached rather than fetched every run.
3. If (b): a check fails if the tier is silently skipped **without** the recorded opt-out — i.e. the
   skip cannot revert to being accidental. Demonstrate by removing the marker and observing RED.
4. Either way, the summary a reader sees distinguishes "this tier was deliberately not run" from
   "this tier passed". No configuration where absence of execution is indistinguishable from success.
5. Portable: the chosen behaviour works in a checkout with no CI provider.

## File impact

`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, `tests/e2e/conftest.py` (the `browser_runner` fixture and its
skip reason), possibly `Makefile` and `tests/e2e/js/package.json`.
data.title: browser_runner tier never executes in CI: chromium is never installed, so the tier silently self-skips and the green is partly vacuous
